I. NICOTINE SPECIFIC MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY

A. Objective: Develop a nicotine monoclonal antibody based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for the determination of nicotine concentrations in samples of interest to PM.

B. Results: A final experiment was conducted to examine the variation within the tobacco ELISA assay using the 10 monitor blends and preparing extracts over a 6 day period. A 250 mg sample of each monitor was extracted in 50 ml of a 1% triethanolamine solution. These data are presently being evaluated by D. Jones and will be reported on at a later date.
A preliminary experiment was conducted to examine the use of 2% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) as a blocking and washing agent for the ELISA assay in place of the 1% Knox gelatin. At this point in time the results indicate that a higher absorbance is obtained with the antibody and less variation observed in the data when BSA is used.

C. Plans: Continue to investigate the use of alternative blocking and washing procedures to decrease the variation within the ELISA assay.

D. References:

1. Crockett, E. A. Notebook No. 9061, pp. 78-105.

2. Dunn, R. L. Notebook No. 9049, pp. 27-43.

II. ELECTROPHORETIC TECHNOLOGY

A. Objective: To develop electrophoretic techniques in house including isoelectric focusing (IEF) and 2-dimensional (2-D) electrophoresis.

B. Results: A liquid phase, preparative iso-electric focusing purified (RF3), bromophenyl blue labeled Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) and a glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) carbamalate sample were run on a Daiichi mini Iso-electric Focusing (IEF) gel (first dimension). Following the IEF dimension, the samples were run in the second dimension on a sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide (SDS) gel using the PhastSystem®. Protein bands were detected at 36 kD (GAPDH) and 67 kD (BSA) which are the reported molecular weights of the two samples.
